Hi Jenna / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the POC moving: 

1) Success criteria (what success looks like):
   - 90%+ intent classification accuracy on your triage prompts (per the evaluation set)
   - Average response latency <350ms p95 on our Dedicated config for target throughput
   - No PII leakage in generation above existing thresholds (we'll run privacy checks)

2) Required inputs from Acme Health:
   - Representative prompt set & historical logs (anonymized) — goal: ~1,000 prompts + 5k historical examples for eval
   - Priority intents and any critical failure modes
   - Technical contact for ingestion and SSO/KMS questions

3) Timeline & ownership (proposed):
   - Feb 19: Acme to share prompt list + sample logs (ideally as CSV/JSONL) — Jenna
   - Feb 20–24: Redwood ingests data, creates eval harness and baseline model runs — Marissa / Nikhil
   - Feb 25: Joint review of initial eval results & tuning plan — all
   - Mar 3: Finalize POC config and start 2-week evaluation window

4) Risks/asks:
   - If logs contain PHI, please confirm anonymization or advise if we should use private deployment for ingestion.
   - Legal: any data processing agreements we need to sign before ingesting logs?

Can you confirm Jenna that you can share the files by EOD Feb 19? If so, please attach as CSV/JSONL and indicate any fields that must be redacted. I've attached a short template for prompt metadata (headers: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_intent, notes).

Thanks — excited to get this going.

—

Hi Jenna — great, thanks for the files. Received the attachments — I see acme_prompts_v1.csv and sample_logs_2026-02.jsonl in your message. 

Answers below: 
1) Throughput: please send expected peak concurrent users and average session length; as a starting point we recommend targeting 100 qps for baseline Dedicated sizing, and we can tune after the first run.
2) Labeling: sampled labeling is fine for an initial eval (we recommend ~1,000 labeled examples across intents). If you have existing labels for some subset, include them — we'll integrate those into the eval harness.

Next actions on our side:
- Nikhil will ingest the files and run an initial data quality pass (schema check, anonymization verification) by Feb 24.
- I'll build the eval harness and run baseline metrics.
- Rishi will prepare a short compliance checklist and confirm if any DPA addendum is necessary prior to full logs ingestion.

If it's helpful, Nikhil can open a shared folder with processed artifacts and the eval notebook link — Marissa to share.

Thanks — expect an update from Nikhil by Feb 24.

—
Marissa

Hi all —

Quick ingest update: I pulled the two attachments Jenna shared and ran a schema + PII scan. Findings: 
- acme_prompts_v1.csv: 500 rows, columns look good (prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_intent, notes). No overt PII detected in prompt_text samples.
- sample_logs_2026-02.jsonl: 500 lines; we verified anonymization of name/email fields but there are free-text fields that could contain PHI. 

Proposed short plan: 
1) Redwood will run automated PHI detection and replace tokens flagged as PHI with [REDACTED] for the POC eval dataset. We will preserve original ids in a separate mapping file stored in your private bucket if you'd like.
2) I'll produce an initial eval harness (intent classification baseline + response fidelity checks) and post results to the shared Drive link by Feb 24 EOD. Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cPOCPlan
3) Rishi, can you confirm if we should proceed with the processed (redacted) logs or wait for Legal to sign the DPA addendum?
